advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread app.state.startup_binding.llm_runtime through _worker into review_and_vote(..., runtime=...) instead of leaving the composed binding unused.
evidence: search of app.py for `runtime=` returned `(no matches)`
app.py:298: `app.state.startup_binding = compose_startup_binding(app.state.config)` is the only use of the binding
commit trailer: 'app: compose the startup binding at lifespan and pass its runtime to each worker'
advisory.finding: The commit message states 'app: compose the startup binding at lifespan and pass its runtime to each worker', but the runtime from app.state.startup_binding is never forwarded to the workers: `_worker` calls `review_and_vote(event, config=cfg, force=force)` with no `runtime=` argument, and no `runtime=` appears anywhere in app.py.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass the composed runtime into _worker (e.g. store it on app.state and forward runtime=app.state.startup_binding.llm_runtime in the review_and_vote call), or drop app.state.startup_binding if per-review recomposition is intended.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the review path consume the single startup-composed runtime rather than recomposing a fresh binding per review in _resolve_review_runtime.
evidence: startup.py docstring: 'composes its NON-SECRET startup policy and its live provider-native LLM binding ONCE, at startup'
advisory.finding: `_resolve_review_runtime` recomposes a fresh StartupBinding on every review when no runtime is passed (`return _startup.compose_startup_binding(cfg).llm_runtime`), which contradicts the module's own 'composed ONCE at startup' contract and defeats the purpose of the app-level app.state.startup_binding.

advisory.finding: Vestigial `if TYPE_CHECKING: pass` block added to app.py imports nothing and is a no-op.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the app worker forwards app.state.startup_binding.llm_runtime into review_and_vote (and wire the worker to actually pass it).
evidence: app.py:218 `async def _worker(queue: asyncio.Queue, cfg: ReceiverConfig)` — worker signature has no runtime and never reads app.state.startup_binding
app.py:298 `app.state.startup_binding = compose_startup_binding(app.state.config)` composes the binding but nothing consumes its llm_runtime
voter.py:464 `runtime = _resolve_review_runtime(runtime, cfg)` composes an equivalent ambient runtime when the caller passes None, masking a dropped app-level forward
ABSENCE: none of the four new test files exercise app.py / _worker forwarding of startup_binding.llm_runtime
advisory.finding: The app worker never forwards the composed startup binding's runtime to review_and_vote (app.py:248 calls it without `runtime=`), yet no test asserts the app composes app.state.startup_binding and threads its llm_runtime into each worker's review_and_vote call. Because _resolve_review_runtime silently composes an equivalent ambient runtime when none is passed, a regression that drops the app→worker forwarding is undetectable — the very cutover the commit message describes ('pass its runtime to each worker') is untested.
scenarios: A future change composes a non-ambient runtime in the binding but the worker keeps calling review_and_vote without it; reviews silently run under the fallback ambient runtime and no test fails
